content.text: Might be nice if this were configurable, so we could turn this off if desired. Right now, we know exactly what the datastream ID is in Fedora 3, and this change sounds like it would introduce some uncertainty about what the exact file/datastream name is in OCFL.
Making this a toggle-able feature seems very appropriate.
It would be good to get
's review of the functionality of the PR as well.
Works for me. I don't think we would turn this on for migrating our objects.
: As you probably observed, the default is "business as usual", i.e. no extensions.
Looks OK to me, although in-line XML datastreams pulled out of the Fedora 3 FOXML and saved as their own XML files are missing XML declarations.
Edited - the XML declaration request has since been written up as FCREPO-3197,

The MIME-to-extension code looks fine.  For the record, if coming from Fedora 3, there is a %FEDORA_HOME%/server/config/mime-to-extensions.xml which could also possibly be leveraged for this application.
I also ran a test, and the extensions flag works as advertised.  I also reviewed the code, it looks fine, issue can be closed.

Migrated datastreams have no file extension.  It would be nice if migrated datastreams have a file extension inferred from the MIME type; e.g. DC.xml instead of just DC, and OCR.txt instead of just OCR.  This should particularly help out with in-line XML datastreams.
